statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 16 because the overnight NQ advance was fully retraced inside a 0.33% band, while Stress stays high at 66 on a 24-year high in the 30-year Treasury yield and a 2014 low in consumer confidence.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON with Tail below the watch threshold. The published forecast marks a narrow danger window from 12:00Z to 16:00Z covering ADP, the August PCE cluster, the U.S. cash open and Chicago PMI, plus a secondary event window around the post-close Micron fiscal Q4 report and its 20:30Z call.
headline: Fully retraced overnight NQ advance keeps Tail low at 16 while a 24-year high in long-end yields holds Stress high
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed at 30,339.33, up 0.21%, inside a contained 0.64% session range of 30,235.67 to 30,429.97, while the broader tape was weaker: the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.09% to 26,797.54, the S&P 500 fell 0.17% to 7,670.84 and the Dow lost 0.26% to 51,349.92. NQ futures reopened at 22:00Z, traded up to 30,737.00 and have since given back the entire advance, quoting 30,644.50 and up 0.10% as of 01:16Z, only 8.50 points above an overnight low of 30,636.00. The whole band spans 0.33% of index level, so the retracement completed rather than failed and no repeated-extension sequence is present. VIX is 16.04, near the low of a 15.73 to 16.44 range. The dominant stressor remains the bond market: the 30-year Treasury yield sits at 5.59% after an intraday 5.62%, its highest since 2002, while the 10-year is 5.26% in a 5.21 to 5.29 range. The 2-year eased to 4.891% from a 4.956% high after New York Fed President John Williams said the Fed did not need to rush its next move, following the September 25 basis point increase; futures still price roughly a 68% chance of a further hike on 28 October. Tuesday's data were soft: Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 81.9 against 89 expected, the lowest since 2014, and JOLTS job openings eased to 7.097 million versus 7.228 million expected. Crude declined more than 2% on improving Saudi supply and an announced release of up to 40 million barrels from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, with WTI at $89.69 and Brent at $96.67 firming only marginally overnight. Asian equities are firm, with the Nikkei 225 up 1.16% at 66,239.80 and the KOSPI up 0.80% at 6,926.08, which conflicts with a fading NQ and argues for lower directional conviction rather than higher Tail. The environment is genuinely difficult, so Stress is held high at 66, but the observed NQ price path is orderly and two-way, so Tail stays low at 16. The forecast raises Tail to a 23 to 24 peak across the 12:00Z to 14:00Z block where ADP, the PCE cluster, the cash open and Chicago PMI land together, and to 20 to 21 around the post-close Micron report, in both cases as conditional event risk rather than observed structure. Shared Finviz context was 131 minutes old and partial at run time, so it was not used as current evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 01:00Z, published Claude Tail opened at 24 during the European morning of 29 September, held 20 to 24 through the U.S. session, then decayed steadily to 16 by the 00:00Z hour as the cash session closed in a contained range and Globex stayed orderly. Stress fell from 78 to 67 over the same window while Confidence held at 87 to 88. The 14:00Z hour on 29 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps Tail at 16 to 19 through the Asian and European sessions on a contained-range assumption, peaks at 23 to 24 across the 12:00Z to 14:00Z block where ADP, the August PCE cluster, the U.S. cash open and Chicago PMI land together, decays to 18 to 20 through the U.S. afternoon, then rises to 20 to 21 around the post-close Micron fiscal Q4 report before easing to 17 by the start of 1 October. Stress stays high throughout because the long-end yield, tightening-odds and consumption backdrop is not resolved by any single print.
